answer: A mailed hardware key ties each agent to a real postal address. First, an operator requests a key and the network ships a small ferrous token, stamped with a one-time code, to a verified address. Second, the operator enters the code within 14 days to activate one agent. Third, each address may hold only two live keys, and any key seen on two agents is revoked. Running 1,000 fake agents means renting 500 mailboxes at about $10 a month plus $4 shipping per key, so over $64,000 a year. Each key is like an anchor sunk under a cedar dock: cheap to set once, ruinous to fake by the hundred.
